title: Por Pia Tod (Thai Crispy Spring Rolls)
description: Por Pia Tod is a popular Thai appetizer featuring crispy golden spring rolls filled with savory meat, vegetables, and glass noodles. Served with a sweet-sour dipping sauce, these rolls are a favorite at Thai restaurants and make a perfect snack or starter.

ingredients.title: Filling
items: Ground pork (or chicken/shrimp/tofu for variation) – 200 g
Glass noodles – 50 g (soaked, drained, cut into 2-inch lengths)
Onion or shallot – 1 small, finely diced

ingredients.title: Wrapping & Frying
items: Spring roll wrappers (8" square, thawed if frozen) – 20
Neutral oil (e.g., rice bran or canola) – for deep frying

ingredients.title: Dipping Sauce (Nam Jim Po Pia)
items: Carrot – 1 tbsp, finely julienned (optional for garnish)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Filling
steps: Heat oil in a wok over medium-high.
Add garlic and onion, stir-fry until fragrant.
Add pork (or protein of choice), cook until just done.
Stir in mushrooms, carrot, cabbage; cook briefly to keep crunch.
Season with oyster sauce, soy, fish sauce, pepper, sugar.
Remove from heat, fold in noodles and bean sprouts.
Let mixture cool completely before wrapping.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Wrap the Rolls
steps: Place one wrapper on a clean surface, diamond-shaped.
Spoon 1–2 tbsp filling near the bottom corner.
Fold bottom corner over filling, tuck sides in snugly.
Roll tightly toward the top; brush edge with egg wash to seal.
Repeat until all filling is used.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Frying
steps: Heat oil to 170–175°C (340–350°F) in a deep pan or fryer.
Fry rolls in small batches until golden and crisp (3–4 minutes).
Drain on paper towels or a rack for best crispness.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Sauce
steps: Combine vinegar, sugar, water in a small pan. Bring to a light simmer until sugar dissolves.
Add fish sauce, chili, carrot garnish. Cool before serving.

servingSuggestions.title: Plating (Restaurant Style)
items: Stack spring rolls diagonally on a rectangular plate.
Serve with a small dipping bowl of sweet-sour chili sauce.
Garnish with microgreens, carved vegetables, or a banana leaf accent for Thai elegance.

chefTips: Keep filling dry: excess moisture makes rolls soggy.
Fry twice (at 160°C then finish at 180°C) for extra crunch if prepping ahead.
Pair with Thai iced tea or a crisp lager for a complete dining experience.
